💬 Deputy Parliament speaker says Hormuz will not return to pre-war status

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad says that the Strait of Hormuz will not return to the conditions that existed before the war, adding that the United States and the Israeli regime have realized the hard way that there was no military solution to reopening the strategic waterway.

Speaking during a virtual open session of parliament on Monday, Nikzad said Iran had sought during the war to use dialogue and explain realities on the ground to convince the “aggressor and delusional enemy” that the Strait of Hormuz will not return to its pre-war status.
​
“Today, the American-Zionist enemy, faced with the strong fist of the Armed Forces, has practically realized that reopening the Strait of Hormuz has no military solution and must submit to the new regional order,” he stressed.
​
Nikzad said Iran had emphasized during talks with Oman, which he described as a friendly and neighboring country, that it recognized no route other than one agreed upon by the two countries.
​
He added that the route designated by Iran’s Armed Forces is the only possible route for ships to transit, provided they complied with conditions set by the Iranian government.
​
“In this path, all branches of the government are obedient to the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces and the wise Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Imam Khamenei, and are committed to implementing his orders,” he added.
​
Turning to the Arbaeen pilgrimage, Nikzad thanked government agencies and service providers for their around-the-clock efforts to facilitate the travel and pilgrimage of nearly 3.4 million Iranians.
​
He also thanked the Iraqi government and people for their hospitality toward Iranian pilgrims during the Arbaeen commemorations.

Crypto Idea

Long-Term investing strategy

When the crypto market is falling, buying feels scary. When it's going up, it feels like you've already missed your chance.

As a result, most people either buy based on emotion or keep waiting for the perfect entry point — and end up doing nothing at all.

But there's a simple way to avoid this problem: invest a fixed amount of money at regular intervals.

This strategy is called DCA (Dollar-Cost Averaging).

You simply choose the asset, the amount you want to invest, and how often you want to buy.

For example:
$50 worth of Bitcoin every week.

When Bitcoin is cheaper, your $50 buys more. When it's more expensive, it buys less. Over time, your average purchase price naturally evens out, and over the course of a few years, it often ends up being better than the average market participant's.

Bybit even has a built-in Auto-Invest bot designed specifically for this strategy. You set it up once — choose your currency, the coin, the investment amount, and the schedule.

After that, your purchases happen automatically, whether it's every day or once a month. The key is to choose a coin you genuinely believe in for the long term.

📌 Transaction Nonces: Why One Stuck Tx Can Block the Next Ones

Main Points
⏺ Wallet transactions are processed in a specific order
⏺ If one transaction gets stuck, later ones may wait behind it
⏺ This post explains why ordering matters and how wallet “traffic jams” happen

1️⃣ What It Is — the network tracks which transaction from an address should come next.
2️⃣ Why It Exists — ordering prevents replay issues and helps the chain process actions correctly.
3️⃣ The Problem — a low-fee transaction can get stuck, blocking later transactions from the same wallet.
4️⃣ User Options — speed it up, replace it, or cancel it with a new transaction using the same nonce.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — don’t fire multiple transactions blindly, and always check fees before signing.

Final Thoughts

In blockchains, the transaction itself matters — but so does its place in line. One weak step can freeze the whole flow after it.

📌 Tether Q2 profit hits $1.5B as USDT supply grows 

⚠️ Tether generated approximately $1.5 billion in net operating profit during the second quarter of 2026 as returns from US Treasury holdings and repo operations supported its earnings. The figures appeared in Tether’s latest reserve attestation, prepared by accounting firm BDO and released Friday. US government-backed securities continued to account for the largest portion of the company’s reserve portfolio. 

🌐 Interest earned from that portfolio, along with returns from repo operations, provided the main source of Tether’s second-quarter profit. The company’s exposure to short-term US debt has made its earnings sensitive to Federal Reserve policy and changes in Treasury yields. Tether also reported that the circulating supply of USDT reached approximately $184.6 billion by the end of June. Based on the company’s figures, the token controlled more than 60% of the global stablecoin market.
